prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: نتائج الانتخابات حسب الدائرة (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 5 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "الدائرة" spans 1 col × 2 row; "المرشح أ" spans 2 col × 1 row; "المرشح ب" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 17px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "الدائرة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 130px
  col 2: header "المرشح أ › الأصوات" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 58px
  col 3: header "المرشح أ › النسبة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 50px
  col 4: header "المرشح ب › الأصوات" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 58px
  col 5: header "المرشح ب › النسبة" · longest unbreakable word 50px · one-line width 50px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 413px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 412px.
Fixed: content, font, 17px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Publication table of election results by district, comparing candidate A and candidate B vote counts and vote shares in each district.","reading":"Right-to-left: identify the district at the far right, then scan candidate A votes and percentage, then candidate B votes and percentage; compare candidates within each row and compare vote/share columns down the table.","groups":["col 1: row identifier (district)","cols 2–3: candidate A block (votes, percentage)","cols 4–5: candidate B block (votes, percentage)","cols 2 and 4: vote counts, same role and should align","cols 3 and 5: percentages, same role and should align"],"keep_intact":["all vote counts such as 21,340 and 13,905","all percentages such as 41.2% and 8.6%","candidate labels المرشح أ and المرشح ب","unbreakable Arabic words in district names"],"may_wrap":["multi-word district names such as دائرة المفرق الأولى","two-level header labels if necessary, but not numeric data cells"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [112, 79, 71, 79, 71] · table 413×395px · row heights [39, 39, 66, 66, 66, 39, 39, 39] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [98, 86, 71, 86, 71] · table 413×474px · row heights [39, 39, 92, 66, 92, 66, 39, 39] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [84, 82, 82, 82, 82] · table 413×553px · row heights [39, 39, 92, 92, 92, 66, 66, 66] · column headers wrapped 0/7 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}

log.raw: {"critique":[{"design":"r0A","good":"This is the only design that hits the real constraint: every vote count and percentage stays on one line, no mid-word splits, and the table is the shortest of the three (395px). The width profile also mirrors the reading hierarchy — widest column for the district identifier, medium for the vote counts, narrowest for the percentages — so the eye can tell votes from shares by proportion alone. District names wrap to two lines, which is an acceptable price for keeping the numbers intact.","problems":"There is zero slack anywhere. The two-line district rows (66px) break the vertical rhythm of the otherwise 39px rows, and the percentage columns look pinched relative to the vote columns right beside them. Column 1 also carries a couple of pixels more than the district text actually needs, while the numeric columns have none to spare.","cause":"Cols 2/4 are 79px and cols 3/5 are 71px — exactly the one-line minimums (58+21 and 50+21). Any subpixel rounding or a hair-wider glyph pushes a figure onto a second line and silently inflates a row. Col 1 at 112px (91px of text) is the maximum the numeric columns permit, so the layout sits on a knife edge with no reserve."},{"design":"r0B","good":"Numbers are comfortable and unambiguously single-line; vote columns at 86px have generous breathing room and the percentage columns stay at their one-line minimum, so at least the roles remain distinguishable by width.","problems":"The district column is now visibly starved: names break into three lines ('دائرة / المفرق / الأولى'), so five of six rows grow to 92px and the table becomes 474px tall — 20% taller than r0A with no gain in legibility. Rows no longer read as units because the identifier occupies more vertical space than the data it labels.","cause":"Col 1 was cut to 98px, leaving only 77px of text width — below the width needed to fit 'دائرة المفرق' on one line. The 7px taken from col 1 were handed to the vote columns (86px), where 79px already sufficed, so the width was spent where it produced nothing."},{"design":"r0C","good":"All numeric cells are safely single-line and the table looks superficially calm and even.","problems":"The worst of the three: every multi-word district name breaks to three lines, the table balloons to 553px, and the rows become tall, airy boxes in which the district label dominates. Equal widths also erase the distinction between identifier, count and share — the reader loses the cue that columns 2 and 4 are the same kind of quantity and 3 and 5 another.","cause":"Forcing all five columns to 82px gives the district column only 61px of text width — barely more than the longest single word — while over-provisioning the percentages (82px for 50px of content) and the votes (82px for 58px). Width was moved from the column that needed it to columns that did not."}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"r1A-trim","widths":[110,79,72,79,72],"change":"Keep r0A's successful structure and shave only 2px from the district column to buy 1px of slack for each percentage column. Districts should still hold at two lines, numbers stay single-line, and the percentages stop sitting at their absolute minimum."},{"name":"r1B-slack","widths":[108,80,72,80,72],"change":"Spread a small reserve across every numeric column (1px each) by taking 4px from the district column. Tests whether a 87px text width still keeps 'دائرة المفرق' on one line; if it does, this is the most robust version against rounding, if it does not, r1A is the answer."},{"name":"r1C-probe","widths":[104,79,74,79,74],"change":"Deliberate boundary probe: push the district column down to 104px (83px of text) to give the percentage columns 3px of slack each. If districts still wrap at two lines this is the most comfortable numeric layout; if they jump to three lines it confirms r0A/r1A's district width is the floor and should be abandoned."}]}
